result.text:
Confirmed cyber incidents & major US outages or those mistaken for hacks disclosed in the first 2 weeks of November 2026.

Confirmed Hacks/Cyber Incidents
1. Optimizely supply-chain attack
Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s web experimentation platform (A/B testing tool) to inject malicious JavaScript into customer sites. It affected ~178 organizations / 188 projects, including major US ones such as CNN, Zoom, HSBC, Salesforce, Equifax, IKEA, Alaska Airlines, Fox News, and others (plus international brands like BBC). The code aimed at credit-card skimming on checkouts, crypto-wallet address swapping, and potential iPhone/iPad exploits on older iOS versions.

2. Vanderbilt University cyberattack
University confirmed an active cybersecurity incident affecting devices, systems, and cloud services.

3. Queens Public Library ransomware
Library confirmed a ransomware attack that disrupted its website, mobile app, on-site public computers, free Wi-Fi, checkout/return machines, and digital media services across all 66 branches in New York City.

4. Access Dental Management data breach
Unauthorized network access allowed viewing/copying of personal and health data (names, addresses, DOB, SSNs, medical/health insurance information).

5. Uber driver data breach via Fireworks AI
Uber confirmed that a third-party AI vendor (Fireworks AI) was breached; compromised credentials were used to access Uber data. Approximately 149,346 drivers were affected. Exposed data included names, addresses, dates of birth, and driver’s license numbers/images.

6. Fandango checkout card-skimmer incident
Fandango confirmed that an unauthorized party could access payment-card data entered on its ticketing checkout page. Exposed fields included card numbers, CVVs, expiration dates, billing ZIP codes, and email addresses. Number of affected customers was not fully disclosed (state filings noted hundreds in places like Oregon/Vermont).

7. ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE-2026-84869) active exploitation
High-severity vulnerability actively exploited against MSP technician workstations and servers. Huntress observed ~688,000 automated attempts across dozens of MSP servers, with at least one successful compromise in seconds. Attackers pushed malicious files via remote sessions.

Major US Outages Mistaken for Cyberattacks:
1. Microsoft 365 outage 
Widespread disruption to Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint, and related services.

2. FAA nationwide ground stop 
Grounded flights across the US (affecting thousands) due to instability in aging air-traffic communications/telecom systems, linked to router/telecom work. 

3. United Airlines technology issue
Delayed departures (hundreds of flights affected for roughly 1–2 hours).

4. Chase & multi-bank transaction disruptions
Chase reported a software bug in on-premises hardware that slowed some transactions; effects rippled to interbank/Zelle activity involving other banks (reports involving Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, etc.).

5. NSA NSANet temporary degradation
Classified internal NSA network experienced temporary degradation.

6. Apple services outage
Disruptions to iCloud, Apple Pay, App Store, and related services for some users.
